about: One origin rule, restated in two packages that may not import each other: the client's binding (isBindableServer, packages/client/src/project.ts) and the issuer check (isServableIssuerUrl, packages/auth/src/server-options.ts) (manifest-h.md §2.8.1).

Two suites hold the whole rule to this file: packages/client/src/project.test.ts holds the binding to every row, and packages/auth/src/server-options.origin-rule.test.ts holds the issuer check to every row, through createAuthOptions, where production asks it. A change to either function is checked against the same rows.

A third suite reads it for the loopback half alone: packages/server/src/security-headers.test.ts holds upgradeInsecureRequestsFor (packages/server/src/security-headers.ts), which drops upgrade-insecure-requests for http on a loopback host, to every row by its scheme and host (H.5).

The rule: https on any host, or http on a loopback host (localhost, *.localhost, 127.0.0.0/8, [::1]); and no user name, password, query or fragment, an empty query (?) and an empty fragment (#) included.

No row has a path. The binding refuses a path and the issuer check does not, so a row with a path would be one on which the two disagree by design; the binding's path refusal is tested in project.test.ts, and the issuer check's acceptance of one in server-options.origin-rule.test.ts.

kind names what a row is there to show. The six refusals manifest-h.md §2.8.1 lists (userinfo, password-only, query, empty-query, fragment, empty-fragment) each appear over https and over loopback http, and project.test.ts holds the file to that; server-options.origin-rule.test.ts holds it to production's issuer, accepted, and to the user name and password rows over both.
